To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human urethra myocytes express T- and L- type Ca2+ channels.
the urethral smooth muscle cells possess currents with electphysiological and pharmacological features of T- and Ca2+ currents.
human urethra contains T- and L- type Ca2+ channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of human smooth muscle cells from urethra.
the development of a novel method for studying the effects of drugs on human urethral smooth muscle.
the electrophysiological characteristics of the human urethral smooth muscle cells, which may provide new insights into the pathogenesis of the lower urinary tract dysfunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ currents recorded from freshly dispersed smooth muscle cell from the human proxim urethra consist of T and L type Ca2+ channels.
Ca2+ channel blockers, such as nifedipin, are likely to be effective in the treatment of urethral hypercontractility, as has been shown in other urogenital smooth muscle tissues.
the T- and L-currents are present in the human urethral smooth muscle cells and the T-currents are more predominant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the urethral myocyte has a Ca2+-dependent mechanism that is sensitive to the concentration of extracellular Mg2+ and that is likely to be important for the control of smooth muscle contraction.
the L current is the main component of the inward current in these cells.
the L current is a high-threshold current that is sensitive to dihydropyridines and is activated by depolarisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the urethral smooth muscle cells have a high expression of L-type Ca2+-channel subtypes.
the urethral smooth muscle cells are very sensitive to the effects of the L-type calcium channel blocker verapamil.
